transformer.title: Attention Is All You Need
transformer.venue: NIPS 2017 / Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30
transformer.version: conference-hosted full PDF downloaded 2026-10-06; not latest arXiv
transformer.read_scope: Full PDF obtained; selectively read architecture §§3.1–3.5 and visually inspected Fig.1 at full page.

code.reason: Paper architecture is authoritative; no code execution or implementation equivalence claimed.

facts.fact: Encoder has six layers, each self-attention then FFN with residual addition and post-LayerNorm. Decoder has six layers with masked self-attention, cross-attention, FFN and three post-norm residual paths.
facts.evidence: PDF pp.2–3 §3.1; visually verified Fig.1 p.3

facts.fact: Encoder output provides cross-attention K/V; decoder stream provides Q. Shifted-right target input and causal mask preserve autoregression. Embeddings receive added positional encoding; decoder feeds linear+softmax.
Base d_model=512, N=6, h=8 and d_ff=2048.

limitations: Source fixture preparation only; no paper reproduction/training/performance experiments.
Original images and source manifests are private evaluation references; only method.md is the drawing-worker handoff.
Complete PDFs acquired, selective architecture reading performed; no claim of complete-paper close reading.

resnet.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
resnet.version: CVF accepted conference version (open-access watermark); full PDF downloaded 2026-10-06
resnet.read_scope: Full PDF obtained; selectively read residual formulation, architecture, normalization and bottleneck subsections; visually inspected Fig.2 and Fig.5 full pages.

code.coverage_limits: Official converted deploy model, not original training code; no complete network execution, kernels, solver or basic-block implementation inspected.

facts.fact: Residual and identity paths merge by elementwise addition before ReLU.
Same-resolution basic example uses 64-channel input and two 3×3,64 layers; bottleneck uses 256-channel input, 1×1,64 then 3×3,64 then 1×1,256.
BN follows each convolution and precedes activation. Original Fig.5 omits BN boxes.
Identity bottleneck res2b takes res2a both into branch2a and directly into Eltwise; the last branch stage ends BN/Scale, merge feeds ReLU.
facts.conditions: Static deploy-definition interpretation; no Caffe execution.

facts.fact: res2a differs: shortcut branch1 is a 1×1 projection to 256. Its residual stages have 64,64,256 outputs.
facts.conditions: Used only as variant contrast; target Fig.5 is identity block.

limitations: Source fixture preparation only; no paper reproduction/training/performance experiments.
Original images and source manifests are private evaluation references; only method.md is the drawing-worker handoff.

unet.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
unet.version: arXiv:1505.04597v1 (18 May 2015), author-linked preprint; not Springer typeset proceedings
unet.read_scope: Full original v1 preprint obtained; selectively read architecture §2 and valid-convolution context; visually inspected Fig.1 full page.

code.reason: Author site advertises 2015-10-02 185MB Caffe release, but bounded task uses original paper only; did not download/inspect release or invent a commit.

facts.fact: Four pools and four up-convolutions; two valid 3×3+ReLU convolutions per stage; cropped encoder features concatenate into each corresponding expanding stage. Final 1×1 maps64 features to classes.
Skip endpoint dimensions568,280,136,64 crop to392,200,104,56; paired maps concatenate across channels, not elementwise sum.
